cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work everywhere; tip 18 to 20 percent at restaurants. Sales tax is added at the till.
name: Denali
tagline: North America's highest peak above wild tundra
summary: Denali National Park is six million acres of tundra, taiga and glaciers below the 6,190-metre summit of Denali. Ride the park bus into the wilderness to spot grizzlies, moose, caribou and wolves, take a flightseeing plane to land on a glacier, and meet the sled dogs at the park kennels.
seasonNote: The park road and buses run late May to mid September; the mountain hides in cloud about two days in three.
arrival: About 4 hours by car or 8 hours by the scenic Alaska Railroad from Anchorage.
gettingAround: Park buses beyond Mile 15; private cars only on the first stretch.
foodTip: Alaskan salmon, halibut and reindeer sausage.
buyTip: Native Alaskan crafts and qiviut wool.
baseArea: Denali Park entrance (Glitter Gulch) or Healy

items.name: Park road bus tour
items.summary: Narrated bus ride into the wilderness looking for grizzlies, caribou and moose.
items.expect: Book months ahead; road may be shortened by a landslide.
items.tip: Sit on the left going in.

items.name: Flightseeing and glacier landing
items.summary: Small plane around the summit with a landing on a glacier.
items.tip: Fly from Talkeetna for better odds.

items.name: Sled dog kennels
items.summary: The only sled dogs used by a US national park, with free demonstrations.

items.name: Savage River Loop
items.summary: Easy riverside walk at the end of the public road.

items.name: Horseshoe Lake Trail
items.summary: Short hike to a lake with beaver dams.

items.name: Nenana River rafting
items.summary: Glacial river rafting through a canyon.

items.name: Talkeetna
items.summary: Quirky climbers' town with the best Denali views.
items.tip: Stop for lunch and the riverbank view.

items.name: Alaskan salmon and halibut
items.summary: Wild salmon and halibut fish and chips.

items.name: Reindeer sausage
items.summary: Smoky sausage served at breakfast or from food trucks.

items.name: 49th State Brewing
items.summary: Brewpub with the bus from Into the Wild outside.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work everywhere; tip 18 to 20 percent at restaurants. Sales tax is added at the till.
name: Hawaii Volcanoes (Hilo)
tagline: Living volcanoes, rainforest and waterfalls on the Big Island
summary: Hilo is the rainy, green side of Hawaiʻi's Big Island, close to Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park. Look into the steaming Kīlauea caldera, walk through the Thurston lava tube, drive the Chain of Craters Road to sea arches, see Rainbow Falls, and climb Mauna Kea for sunset above the clouds.
seasonNote: Hilo is rainy all year, wettest November to March; check eruption status before visiting.
arrival: Hilo International is 10 minutes from town; Kona is 2 hours away.
gettingAround: A rental car; buses are infrequent.
foodTip: Loco moco, poke, malasadas and shave ice.
buyTip: Kona coffee, macadamia nuts and local art.

items.name: Kīlauea caldera
items.summary: Overlooks into the steaming crater of one of the world's most active volcanoes.
items.tip: Come back after dark if lava is glowing.

items.name: Thurston lava tube
items.summary: Walk through a 500-year-old lava cave in fern forest.

items.name: Chain of Craters Road
items.summary: Scenic road down past craters and lava flows to a sea arch.
items.tip: Stop at the Hōlei Sea Arch.

items.name: Rainbow Falls
items.summary: Waterfall where morning sun makes rainbows in the mist.

items.name: ʻAkaka Falls
items.summary: 135-metre waterfall on a rainforest loop.

items.name: Mauna Kea summit
items.summary: Sacred mountain and observatories above the clouds.

items.name: Liliʻuokalani Gardens
items.summary: Japanese garden on Hilo Bay.

items.name: Loco moco
items.summary: Rice, burger patty, fried egg and gravy, invented in Hilo.

items.name: Poke
items.summary: Raw ahi tuna marinated with shoyu and seaweed.
items.tip: Buy by the pound at a market.

items.name: Hilo Farmers Market
items.summary: Tropical fruit, malasadas and crafts.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work everywhere; tip 18 to 20 percent at restaurants. Sales tax is added at the till.
name: Page (Antelope Canyon)
tagline: Slot canyons and the Horseshoe Bend
summary: Page is a small desert town beside Lake Powell surrounded by some of the Southwest's most photographed places. Walk through the glowing light beams of Antelope Canyon with a Navajo guide, peer down at the Colorado River curling round Horseshoe Bend, and take a boat or kayak into Lake Powell's red-rock canyons.
seasonNote: Light beams in Upper Antelope are best from April to September around midday; summer is very hot.
arrival: About 4.5 hours from Las Vegas, 2.5 hours from the Grand Canyon South Rim.
gettingAround: A car; canyons require Navajo-guided tours.
foodTip: Navajo tacos, Southwestern BBQ and Mexican food.

items.name: Antelope Canyon
items.summary: Narrow sandstone slot canyon lit by light beams.
items.expect: Guided tours only; book weeks ahead.
items.tip: Upper for beams, Lower for ladders and fewer crowds.

items.name: Horseshoe Bend
items.summary: Colorado River loops 300 metres below a cliff edge.

items.name: Lake Powell boat tour
items.summary: Boat through red-rock canyons of a huge reservoir.
items.tip: Rent a kayak for Antelope Canyon by water.

items.name: Glen Canyon Dam
items.summary: Massive dam with a visitor centre and bridge views.

items.name: The Wave and Coyote Buttes
items.summary: Swirling sandstone formation reached by permit lottery only.

items.name: Toadstool Hoodoos
items.summary: Short hike to balanced rock hoodoos.

items.name: Navajo tacos
items.summary: Fry bread piled with chili and toppings.

items.name: Southwestern BBQ
items.summary: Smoked brisket and ribs.

items.name: Mexican food
items.summary: Tacos and enchiladas.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work everywhere; tip 18 to 20 percent at restaurants. Sales tax is added at the till.
name: Monument Valley
tagline: Red buttes of the American West on Navajo land
summary: Monument Valley is a Navajo Tribal Park of towering red sandstone buttes, the backdrop to countless Westerns. Drive the 17-mile Valley Drive, take a Navajo-guided tour to hidden arches, watch sunrise over the Mittens, and stand at Forrest Gump Point on the road in.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are mild; winter can bring snow on the buttes.
arrival: About 2 hours from Page and 6 hours from Las Vegas.
gettingAround: A car for the Valley Drive; guided jeep tours for restricted areas.
foodTip: Navajo fry bread and mutton stew.
buyTip: Navajo silver jewellery and pottery from roadside stalls.
baseArea: The View Hotel or Goulding's Lodge

items.name: Valley Drive
items.summary: 17-mile dirt loop past the Mittens, Merrick Butte and John Ford's Point.

items.name: Navajo-guided jeep tour
items.summary: Guided tour into restricted areas with arches and petroglyphs.

items.name: Mittens sunrise
items.summary: Sun rising between the East and West Mittens.
items.tip: Stay at The View for balcony sunrise.

items.name: Forrest Gump Point
items.summary: Long straight road to the buttes where Forrest stopped running.

items.name: Wildcat Trail
items.summary: Self-guided 3-mile loop around West Mitten.

items.name: Goosenecks State Park
items.summary: San Juan River's deep winding meanders.

items.name: Navajo fry bread
items.summary: Fry bread from Navajo stalls.

items.name: The View Restaurant
items.summary: Restaurant facing the Mittens.
items.tip: Get a window table at sunset.

items.name: Goulding's Stagecoach Restaurant
items.summary: Historic trading post restaurant used by John Ford.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work everywhere, even at markets. Tipping is optional.
name: Darwin and Kakadu
tagline: Tropical frontier city and gateway to Kakadu
summary: Darwin is Australia's tropical northern capital, a relaxed harbour city close to some of the country's greatest wilderness. Shop the Mindil Beach sunset market, swim in the croc-free waterholes of Litchfield, see 20,000-year-old rock art and saltwater crocodiles in Kakadu, and learn the city's WWII history.
seasonNote: The dry season, May to October, is best; wet season brings storms and closes some roads but waterfalls roar.
arrival: Darwin International is 15 minutes from the city.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; rent a car or 4x4 for Litchfield and Kakadu.

items.name: Mindil Beach Sunset Market
items.summary: Thursday and Sunday market with food stalls and sunset over the sea.

items.name: Litchfield National Park
items.summary: Waterfalls and swimming holes plus magnetic termite mounds.
items.tip: Swim at Wangi and Florence Falls.

items.name: Kakadu National Park
items.summary: UNESCO park with Aboriginal rock art at Ubirr and Nourlangie and crocodile cruises on Yellow Water.

items.name: Museum and Art Gallery of the NT
items.wiki: Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory
items.summary: Aboriginal art, Cyclone Tracy exhibit and Sweetheart the crocodile.

items.name: Crocosaurus Cove
items.summary: Swim in a cage beside giant saltwater crocodiles.

items.name: WWII Oil Tunnels and Darwin Military Museum
items.summary: History of the 1942 bombing of Darwin.

items.name: Waterfront Precinct and Wave Lagoon
items.summary: Croc-free swimming lagoon and harbour restaurants.

items.name: Barramundi
items.summary: Local barra grilled or battered.

items.name: Parap Market laksa
items.summary: Saturday market famous for laksa.

items.name: Mindil market food
items.summary: Asian and Aussie food stalls by the beach.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work everywhere; tipping isn't expected.
name: Wanaka
tagline: Lakeside alpine town, quieter twin of Queenstown
summary: Wanaka is a relaxed lakeside town at the edge of Mount Aspiring National Park. Photograph the lone willow in the lake, climb Roys Peak for one of New Zealand's best views, hike to the Rob Roy Glacier, ski at Cardrona and Treble Cone, and fly over to Milford Sound.
seasonNote: Summer is for hiking; June to September is ski season.
arrival: About 1 hour by car from Queenstown Airport.
gettingAround: A car is best; town is walkable.
foodTip: Lamb, Central Otago pinot noir and craft beer.

items.name: That Wanaka Tree
items.summary: A lone willow growing in the lake, New Zealand's most photographed tree.

items.name: Roys Peak
items.summary: Steep 16 km hike to a ridge above Lake Wanaka.
items.expect: Closed for lambing Oct to Nov.

items.name: Rob Roy Glacier Track
items.summary: Valley hike to a hanging glacier with waterfalls.

items.name: Puzzling World
items.summary: Leaning tower, illusion rooms and a maze.

items.name: Cardrona Alpine Resort
items.summary: Family ski field in winter, mountain biking in summer.

items.name: Milford Sound scenic flight
items.summary: Flight over the Southern Alps to the fiord.

items.name: Mount Iron
items.summary: Short hike with 360-degree views over the lake.

items.name: Central Otago pinot noir
items.summary: Lakeside vineyards like Rippon with famous views.

items.name: New Zealand lamb
items.summary: Slow-cooked or grilled local lamb.

items.name: Wanaka craft beer
items.summary: Local breweries and beer gardens.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted now, but some bars, bakeries and apple-wine taverns are still cash only. Round up tips by about 10 percent.
name: Frankfurt
tagline: Skyscrapers, apple wine and Germany's gateway
summary: Frankfurt is Germany's banking capital and biggest air hub, where glass towers rise above a rebuilt medieval core. Stand in the half-timbered Römerberg square, ride up the Main Tower, walk the riverside Museum Embankment, drink apple wine in Sachsenhausen taverns, and take a day trip to the Rhine Valley's castles.
seasonNote: Summer has riverside festivals; the Christmas market runs late November to December.
arrival: Frankfurt Airport is 15 minutes by S-Bahn to the centre.
gettingAround: U-Bahn, S-Bahn and trams; the centre is walkable.
foodTip: Apple wine, green sauce, Handkäse and Frankfurter sausages.
buyTip: Apple wine jugs (Bembel) and Zeil shopping.
baseArea: Altstadt, Sachsenhausen or near the Hauptbahnhof

items.name: Römerberg and the new Altstadt
items.summary: Half-timbered square and rebuilt old town lanes around the town hall.

items.name: Main Tower
items.summary: Open-air platform 200 metres up among the skyscrapers.

items.name: Frankfurt Cathedral
items.summary: Gothic cathedral where emperors were crowned.

items.name: Museumsufer and Städel

items.tip: Saturday flea market on the bank.

items.name: Goethe House
items.summary: Birthplace of Germany's great writer.

items.name: Palmengarten

items.name: Rhine Valley day trip

items.tip: Rüdesheim to St Goar by boat.

items.name: Apple wine taverns in Sachsenhausen
items.summary: Cosy taverns pouring tart apple wine from a stoneware Bembel.
items.tip: Order a Schoppen and sit at shared tables.

items.summary: Cold herb sauce with boiled eggs and potatoes.
